transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-15 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (CSM), Omar (SE), Sofia (Lyra Head of ML), Greg (Platform), Priya (CFO)

Summary: quick QBR, multi-topic; some audio dropouts at 00:34, occasional transcription hiccups.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time for the QBR. quick intro - jordan from Redwood, maya on cs, omar our se,
[00:10] Sofia: hi all, thanks, pretty tight agenda - cost, reliability, then roadmap stuff, then next steps,
[00:20] Greg: yep, and priya's on to watch the spend side, so i'll let her chime in when needed,
[00:30] Priya: hi! thanks.
[00:40] Jordan: cool, jump in. first, usage - we've been seeing Lyra's monthly token consumption up about 32% q/q, most of the increase is embeddings for search indexing and fine-turn chat sessions - omar, i'll let you give details?
[00:52] Omar: yeah so our logs show heavy bursts around 11:00 - 13:00 UTC and again 02:00 UTC, bursts are primarily short multi-turn sessions, embedding jobs run nightly but they've also started to run ad-hoc during the day for re-indexing, that pushes your egress and token tally,
[01:10] Sofia: correct, we had a product push that triggered re-embedding new content and that wasn't throttled, we should've queued it,
[01:20] Jordan: on the cost side we sliced the bill by model and route - looks like the generic chat route is 46% of spend, embeddings 28%, rerank and misc the rest. Priya, does that align with your internal numbers?
[01:34] Priya: roughly, yes. the CFO team is concerned about the month-on-month growth; we need concrete levers, so anything that saves 10-20% is interest,
[01:44] Jordan: understood. quick levers: batching, KV cache for repeated prefixes, cheaper model variants for lower-criticality routes, and quantization on Dedicated can drop per-token costs. note that batching helps but can slightly increase p95 latency - omar can show the tradeoff,
[02:00] Omar: yeah exactly. on Hosted we do smart batching with small windows; on Dedicated you can tune batch window and get more aggressive batching plus int8 quant profiles. from our internal tests int8 quant + batching gave 18-30% cost reduction depending on sequence length.
[02:18] Greg: any hit to output quality from int8?
[02:22] Omar: minimal for most completion use-cases, more noticeable on long form or very technical contexts - but we can A/B test on a canary route,
[02:30] Sofia: can canaryting be limited to non-production? we can't risk user-facing regressions,
[02:36] Maya: yes, canary A/B or gradual rollout with automatic rollback on eval regressions - we have the eval harness and quality monitors, we'll set thresholds you define,
[02:46] Jordan: moving to reliability - you've reported tail latency spikes during your 11-13:00 window - do you have sample traces?
[02:54] Greg: we've got traces; average p50 is fine, but p95 and p99 spike, sometimes up to 1.2s higher than baseline, causing UI stalls.
[03:06] Omar: likely due to bursty traffic and KV cache cold-starts; also some of the calls hit a larger context length than expected which pulls heavier kernels. on Dedicated we can reserve extra capacity to lower queueing and mitigate tail. also prefix caching and warmed KV cache reduce token generation latency,
[03:24] Sofia: what's the expected improvement if we move to a Dedicated pool with reserved capacity? numbers?
[03:30] Omar: from similar customers we typically see 20-40% reduction in p95/p99 when traffic is isolated and GPU scheduling overhead is removed, depends on hit-rate and batching. we'll provide a benchmark plan,
[03:40] Priya: cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[03:44] Jordan: Dedicated has a fixed capacity commitment; effective unit cost usually lower at high throughput, but you pay for reserved nodes. we modeled Lyra's recent month and estimated breakeven at ~10-12M tokens/month depending on burstiness and whether you need SLAs, i'll send the detailed model,
[03:59] Priya: perfect, need that to compare to current spend projection,
[04:06] Sofia: any compliance concerns for us - we have EU customers and data residency requirements, plus SOC2 controls,
[04:12] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II, ISO docs, and private/VPC deployment options with customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations. for Lyra we recommended VPC peering + private control plane if you want full separation; we can share the checklist,
[04:28] Greg: SSO and RBAC? we need SAML integration and granular role permissions for our platform team,
[04:34] Jordan: SAML SSO is supported, plus role-based edges in the console - can lock down keys and routes,
[04:40] Sofia: great.
[04:44] Jordan: roadmap alignment - Lyra mentioned wanting better throughput for embeddings and lower per-token cost, we have planned improvements in our optimizer to improve batching heuristics and auto-quant profiles scheduled Q4 '25,
[04:58] Omar: also pushing kernel-level improvements for long context efficiency, that should reduce cost for long-doc embeddings by around 10-15% in our tests,
[05:06] Sofia: timeline on those features?
[05:09] Omar: early rollouts Q4 2025, wider release in Q1 2026, but we can run private builds for pilot customers earlier under NDA,
[05:18] Priya: if private builds help speed up savings, that's interesting, what's the procurement path?
[05:22] Jordan: standard enterprise addendum, plus private deployment contract; maya will own the compliance docs and procurement touchpoint,
[05:30] Maya: yes i'll coordinate with your procurement and legal, and we'll provide a checklist and timelines,
[05:34] Sofia: one operational ask - can we get daily KV cache hit-rate metrics and batching statistics? that's the quickest debugging telemetry for us,
[05:42] Omar: yep we can enable per-route telemetry and push to your monitoring; will need an internal ticket from Greg to enable log forwarding and sample windows,
[05:52] Greg: i'll open the ticket after this call, include sample logs for the 11-13 window,
[05:58] Jordan: great. quick note on experiments: suggest converting low-criticality routes to a cheaper model (redwood-moderate or community model) and run offline evals to check regressions,
[06:10] Sofia: yes that plus batching seems low-risk, good place to start,
[06:14] Priya: ok finance needs a conservative 3-6 month forecast if we start these optimizations, could you produce sensitivity analysis?
[06:22] Jordan: yes i'll deliver a forecast with optimistic/median/pessimistic scenarios, based on two levers: batching adoption rate and embeddings scheduling, due 2025-10-17,
[06:32] Sofia: any security testing required before private build?
[06:36] Maya: typically pen test and key rotation policy review; we'll provide details and a timeline,
[06:42] Jordan: wrap-up and next steps - recap who does what,
[06:45] Priya: quick question, are there any competitors' offers we should be aware of for price matching?
[06:51] Jordan: anthopic and openai are doing similar things; we can provide comparative unit economics but each vendor's SLA/feature set differs. we focus on predictable inference economics and the private options,
[07:03] Sofia: ok, let's park vendor comparison for now, focus on internal levers,
[07:07] Jordan: noted.
[07:09] [00:07:09] -- mid-call noise -- some words dropped --
[07:20] Omar: technical note: if you choose Dedicated, consider enabling pre-warm kernels during your peak window and sticky routing by customer segment, reduces cold-starts,
[07:30] Greg: how do we validate quality before rollout?
[07:33] Omar: we can set up canary with evaluation suite tied to production prompts; automatic rollback on regression exceeding threshold, and human review for edge cases,
[07:43] Sofia: want to see example eval reports,
[07:46] Maya: will attach a sample eval and the monitoring dashboard to the follow-up notes,
[07:52] Jordan: financial ask - priya, do you need a committed quote for Dedicated?
[07:56] Priya: yes, if we can see a 15% or better unit cost reduction we're open to a 12-month commitment but need flexibility for peak months,
[08:06] Jordan: we can model flexible burst capacity and demonstrate pricing options in the quote,
[08:12] Sofia: anything else on roadmap alignment?
[08:15] Omar: we're also tracking kernel optimizations and batching heuristics; i'll include expected impact numbers in the benchmark doc,
[08:24] Jordan: ok let's move to close - recap next steps and owners: jordan send cost breakdown and forecast, omar run the latency benchmarks, maya send compliance docs, greg share logs.
[08:35] Priya: thanks everyone, sounds like a plan,
[08:38] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and schedule the benchmark.
[08:42] [END]

Call artifacts referenced:
- QBR slide deck (shared) - link: https://redwood.example.com/share/qbr/lyra-2025-10
- Benchmark template (will be shared)
- SOC2 & private deployment checklist (Maya to attach)

Recap (verbatim-ish):
- Immediate wins: batching + schedule embedding jobs off-peak, cheaper model for low-criticality routes -> target 10-20% savings.
- Reliability path: Dedicated reserved pool + KV cache warmers -> 20-40% p95/p99 improvements in similar customers.
- Compliance: private/VPC option + KMS/HSM integrations available; Maya to send docs.
- Next: Jordan send cost forecast & per-model recommendations (due 2025-10-17); Omar run Dedicated benchmarks (due 2025-10-22); Greg to share logs (due 2025-10-16).

End of transcript.
